updated_content: Bare-metal: single loop, no OS scheduler; suitable when the workload is stable, latency-sensitive, and tightly bounded, because the developer owns task ordering and there is no scheduler-induced jitter. RTOS: preemptive multitasking with scheduling guarantees; better when systems must multiplex tasks with bounded worst-case latency, priority inheritance, and deadline-aware dispatch, but scheduler behavior introduces determinism trade-offs the original answer did not explain.
